resposta:
Here are the winners of **The Game Awards 2024** (the 24th edition, held on December 12, 2024 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles):

**Major Categories**
- **Game of the Year:** *Astro Bot* (Team Asobi / Sony Interactive Entertainment)  
- **Best Game Direction:** *Astro Bot*  
- **Best Narrative:** *Metaphor: ReFantazio* (Studio Zero / Sega)  
- **Best Score and Music:** *Final Fantasy VII Rebirth* (Square Enix)  
- **Best Performance:** Melina Juergens as Senua (*Senua’s Saga: Hellblade II*)  
- **Best Independent Game:** *Balatro* (LocalThunk / Playstack)  
- **Best Debut Indie Game:** *Balatro*  
- **Best Ongoing Game:** *Helldivers II* (Arrowhead Game Studios / Sony Interactive Entertainment)  
- **Best VR/AR Game:** *Batman: Arkham Shadow* (Camouflaj / Oculus Studios)  
- **Best Action/Adventure Game:** *Black Myth: Wukong* (Game Science)  
- **Best Role Playing Game:** *Metaphor: ReFantazio*  
- **Best Fighting Game:** *Tekken 8* (Bandai Namco Studios / Arika)  
- **Best Family Game:** *Astro Bot*  
- **Best Sports/Racing Game:** *EA Sports FC 25* (EA Vancouver / EA Sports)  
- **Best Multiplayer Game:** *Helldivers II*  
- **Best Adaptation:** *Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown* (Ubisoft Montpellier / Ubisoft)  

**Esports & Creators**
- **Best Esports Game:** *League of Legends* (Riot Games)  
- **Best Esports Athlete:** Faker (Samsung Galaxy)  
- **Best Esports Team:** T1 (League of Legends)  
- **Content Creator of the Year:** CaseOh (IlloJuan)  

**Honorary & Special Awards**
- **Game Changer Award:** Amir Satvat (T1) – for helping laid‑off game developers find jobs  
- **Games for Impact:** *Neva* (Nomada Studio / Devolver Digital)  
- **Most Anticipated Game:** *Grand Theft Auto VI*  
- **Players’ Voice:** *Black Myth: Wukong*  

**Other Notable Winners**
- **Innovation in Accessibility:** *Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown*  
- **Best Adaptation:** *Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown* (also won Games for Impact)  

*Source: [The Game Awards 2024 – Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024)*

# The Game Awards 2024

Video game awards show

| The Game Awards 2024 | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/a/a9/The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg/250px-The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Game_Awards_2024_poster.jpg) | |
| Date | December 12, 2024 (2024-12-12) |
| Venue | [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater"), Los Angeles |
| Country | United States |

| Most nominations | *Astro Bot**[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_VII_Rebirth "Final Fantasy VII Rebirth")* (7) |
| [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") | *Astro Bot* |
| Website | [thegameawards.com](https://thegameawards.com/rewind/year-2024) |
| Online coverage | |
| Runtime | 3 hours, 12 minutes |
| Viewership | 154 million |

| Directed by | Richard Preuss |
| ← [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023") **·**   [The Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards")   **·** [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "The Game Awards 2025") → | |

**The Game Awards 2024** was an award show to honor the best [video games of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2024 "Video games of 2024"). It was the eleventh show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), and held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024, and [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [d4vd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D4vd "D4vd"), [Royal & the Serpent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_&_the_Serpent "Royal & the Serpent"), [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg"), and [Twenty One Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_One_Pilots "Twenty One Pilots"), and presentations from celebrity guests including [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford"), [Hideo Kojima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideo_Kojima "Hideo Kojima"), and [Aaron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Paul "Aaron Paul").

*[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* and *[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_VII_Rebirth "Final Fantasy VII Rebirth")* led the nominees with seven each, and the former led the show with four wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year"). The inaugural Game Changer award honored [Amir Satvat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amir_Satvat "Amir Satvat") for helping workers in the industry find jobs amid [mass layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022–2025_video_game_industry_layoffs "2022–2025 video game industry layoffs"). Several new games were announced, including *[Elden Ring Nightreign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Nightreign "Elden Ring Nightreign")*, *[Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergalactic:_The_Heretic_Prophet "Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet")*, and *[The Witcher IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witcher_IV "The Witcher IV")*. The show was viewed by over 154 million streams, the most in its history to date.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) Journalists praised the game announcements, developer speeches, and deserving winners, though the eligibility of [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") led to mixed responses.

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2024 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"). He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2) while Richard Preuss returned as director and LeRoy Bennett as creative director and production designer,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) and Michael E. Peter joined as co-executive producer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) The presentation, celebrating the show's tenth anniversary, took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles on December 12, 2024,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3) including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-7) Alternative live streams offering [American Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language") and [audio descriptions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_description "Audio description") were also available on YouTube.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Nominees-3)

The 2024 stage featured more [LED displays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LED_displays "LED displays") than its predecessors, an intentional choice by Bennett to change the show's look each year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Preview-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesHub_How-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-FAQ-9) Public tickets became available for purchase on November 1.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Date-6) Future Class organizer Emily Bouchac indicated that the Future Class initiative—an annual list of 50 individuals from the industry who best represent its future, introduced in 2020—would not induct new members in 2024, instead focusing on valuing existing alumni.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-10)

### Announcements

Preceding the Game Awards, several announcements were made during broadcasts by Wholesome Games and the Latin American Games Showcase on December 10,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Wholesome-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Showcases-12) and [Day of the Devs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_of_the_Devs "Day of the Devs") and the Women-Led Games Showcase on December 11.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Showcases-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_Devs-13) Fewer film and television announcements were made during the Game Awards 2024, instead focusing almost primarily on games; a preview for *[Squid Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_Game "Squid Game")*'s [second season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_Game_season_2 "Squid Game season 2") was aired, but considered secondary to the promotion of the game *Squid Game: Unleashed*.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Hollywood-14) Announcements on released and upcoming games were made for:[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_Live-15)

To promote its own game without the budget necessary for the Game Awards, Pengonauts Studio created its own humorous show with Joystick Ventures: the Game Awards for Games Who Can't Afford the Game Awards (TGAGWCAGA). The ceremony on December 13 showcased more than 70 games out of 600 submitted, with specific award names like "Most Likely to Make You Quit Your Job and Become an Artist".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_TGAGWCAGA-16)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Bleeding_Cool_TGAGWCAGA-17)

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 18, 2024.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Nominees-19) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 22 was eligible for consideration,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) including [downloadable content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downloadable_content "Downloadable content") (DLC), expansions, [remakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remake "Video game remake"), [remasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_remaster "Video game remaster"), and seasonal content.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21) The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 130 media outlets globally;[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Hardcore_Gamer_Nominees-22) ballots were due by November 12.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Eligibility-20) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and on [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-24) until December 11.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Deadline_Nominees-2)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Nominees-25) The exception was the publicly-voted Players' Voice, for which voting opened on December 2.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-26) Specialized juries decided nominees for categories like accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Nominees-27) Two awards—Best Esports Coach and Best Esports Event—were discontinued,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Sheep_Esports-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-India_Today-29) while an additional honorary award, Game Changer, was introduced.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Game_Changer-30) Approximately 112 million public votes were cast overall, a 25% increase from [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023 "The Game Awards 2023").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Viewers-31)

As with the preceding year, the Game Awards partnered with map developer Studio 568 and artists Nighttimes and Spiral House to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, allowing players to vote from November 25 to December 11 for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees selected by Keighley and his team; the winner was announced during the ceremony.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Fortnite-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Epic_Fortnite-33) The hub world opened with a [photorealistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photorealistic "Photorealistic") "MetaHuman" model of Keighley,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34) for which he was scanned in to [Unreal Editor for Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unreal_Editor_for_Fortnite "Unreal Editor for Fortnite") at [3Lateral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3Lateral "3Lateral") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Fortnite-35) Several critics found the model strange and [uncanny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncanny "Uncanny").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Fortnite-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Fortnite-36)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Fortnite-37) Keighley saw the event as "a prototype" for blending the Game Awards and in-game worlds.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GameSpot_Fortnite-38)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on December 12, 2024.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Winners-39) *[Astro Bot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astro_Bot "Astro Bot")* became the third game published by [Sony Interactive Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Interactive_Entertainment "Sony Interactive Entertainment") to win [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") (after *[God of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_of_War_(2018_video_game) "God of War (2018 video game)")* in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2018 "The Game Awards 2018") and *[The Last of Us Part II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_of_Us_Part_II "The Last of Us Part II")* in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2020 "The Game Awards 2020")); its nomination marked Sony's ninth consecutive year in the category and thirteenth nomination overall.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_PlayStation-40) It was the second Best Family Game nominee to win the top prize (after *[It Takes Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Takes_Two_(video_game) "It Takes Two (video game)")* in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41) *[Balatro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balatro "Balatro")* was the first solo-developed Game of the Year nominee (and second card game after *[Hearthstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearthstone "Hearthstone")* in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2014 "The Game Awards 2014")),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Balatro-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Balatro-43) while *[Black Myth: Wukong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Myth:_Wukong "Black Myth: Wukong")* was the first Chinese-developed nominee[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Nominees-44) and *[Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elden_Ring_Shadow_of_the_Erdtree "Elden Ring Shadow of the Erdtree")* was the first DLC to be nominated.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NPR_Nominees-45)

## Reception

### Nominees

Several games saw increased weekly sales following their nominations, including *Final Fantasy VII Rebirth* by 268% and *Metaphor: ReFantazio* by 172%,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Sales-83) and *Balatro* had its second-highest-earning week on mobile and a 100% increase in [concurrent players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrent_players "Concurrent players") on Steam.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PocketGamer_Balatro-84)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PCGamesN_Balatro-85)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Balatro-86) *Balatro*'s nominations pleasantly surprised critics due to its genre,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89) though some felt other [indie games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_games "Indie games") remained overlooked outside of their dedicated categories.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Analysis-90) *[TheGamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheGamer "TheGamer")*'s Stacey Henley appreciated that Games for Impact "can finally feel like part of the show" as, unlike previous years, some of its nominees were also named in other categories,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-91) though *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s Keza MacDonald found its nominees incongruous and criteria confusing.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Nominees-92) Some felt three of the five Players' Voice nominees being [gacha games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gacha_game "Gacha game") justified the lack of more audience-voted categories.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Dot_Esports_Voice-94)

The omission of Future Class was criticized; *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur called it "a loss for the industry",[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Future_Class-95) and *[Digital Trends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Trends "Digital Trends")*'s Giovanni Colantonio considered it a troubling indication that Keighley was attempting to avoid controversy and placate the audience in light of an open letter written by Future Class inductees before the 2023 ceremony.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) Some critics were puzzled by *[Silent Hill 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2_(2024_video_game) "Silent Hill 2 (2024 video game)")*'s Best Narrative nomination as it is a remake of [a 2001 game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_Hill_2 "Silent Hill 2").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Snubs-89)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96) *[Dragon Age: The Veilguard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_Age:_The_Veilguard "Dragon Age: The Veilguard")*, *[EA Sports College Football 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports_College_Football_25 "EA Sports College Football 25")*, and *[The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Zelda:_Echoes_of_Wisdom "The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom")* were considered among the biggest snubs by some critics and viewers.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Shacknews_Snubs-98)

Many journalists and viewers criticized *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree*'s Game of the Year nomination as it overshadowed other games,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Snubs-87)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100) though some felt it was justified by its quality and size.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-AV_Club_DLC-96)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Deserves-101) The show's website was updated before nominees were announced to clarify DLC's eligibility, which many predicted was in preparation for *Shadow of the Erdtree*'s divisive nominations;[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_DLC-21)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_DLC-100)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_DLC-102) some viewers erroneously accused Keighley of changing the rules to make it eligible.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Rules-103) Others also felt its eligibility meant DLC was snubbed at previous shows, like *[Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077:_Phantom_Liberty "Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty")* and *[Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenoblade_Chronicles_3:_Future_Redeemed "Xenoblade Chronicles 3: Future Redeemed")* in 2023,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-104)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Destructoid_DLC-105)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Nintendo_Life_DLC-106) and suggested a new category dedicated to DLC would be more appropriate,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-88)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_GOTY-107)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesRadar_DLC-108) though *TheGamer*'s Henley argued there are too few annual releases to justify it.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_DLC-109)

Some journalists considered *Black Myth: Wukong* an [outlier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlier "Outlier") in the Game of the Year nominees and were surprised by its success;[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Snubs-97)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_GOTY-99) it is the lowest-scoring Game of the Year nominee in the show's history, with 81 out of 100 on [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_Metacritic-110)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Metacritic-111) *TheGamer*'s Tessa Kaur felt the game's biggest accomplishment was its popularity, comparing it to *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*'s [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") nomination at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Wukong-112) Conversely, *[Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_(magazine) "Vice (magazine)")*'s Dwayne Jenkins criticized journalists who questioned its deservedness based solely on its critical reception, despite the positive player response; he argued that such discussions are more appropriate for audiences rather than journalists, who should serve as [neutral intermediaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journalistic_objectivity "Journalistic objectivity"), since the awards have no objective criteria.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Vice_Wukong-113)

### Ceremony

*[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")*'s Gene Park called the 2024 ceremony "the best show put on by the Game Awards so far this decade", though he felt the categories required better curation,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114) and *[Engadget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engadget "Engadget")*'s Mat Smith wrote that "the Game Awards delivered".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) *[VentureBeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VentureBeat "VentureBeat")*'s [Dean Takahashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Takahashi "Dean Takahashi") thought Keighley "redeemed himself" after criticism of the previous ceremony,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Review-49) and *[Push Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Square "Push Square")*'s Sammy Barker felt he deserved credit for responding to past criticism, even if some problems remained.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Review-116) *Digital Trends*'s Colantonio called it "the best possible version" of the show, though he criticized the relegation of important awards to the preshow.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93) *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*'s Issy van der Velde similarly criticized that the esports winners were announced in quick succession during the preshow without acceptance speeches,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) and *TheGamer*'s Kaur felt the show remained too long and padded with boring advertisements, though found the reveals surprising "for the first time in a long time".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Surprises-118)

Journalists deemed the winners deserving, including *Astro Bot*'s Game of the Year award considering its polished and joyful gameplay;[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Polygon_GOTY-41)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115) the game's sales saw an increase after its win, according to estimates published by Alinea Analytics.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Alinea-119) Many writers considered the game announcements surprising and among the best to date;[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Engadget_After-115)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) *The Guardian*'s MacDonald compared it to "an old-school [E3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E3 "E3") conference".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Guardian_Review-120) Viewers responded negatively to *[Catly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catly "Catly")*'s reveal trailer;[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Catly-121)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Catly-122) the developer denied claims of [generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") and [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") technology, and shared a draft version of the trailer with journalists.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-IGN_Catly-123)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Developer_Catly-124)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Catly_2-125) The musical performances were praised;[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Arcane-126) *[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")*'s Surej Singh called the *Arcane* performance an "emotional and stirring medley".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Arcane-126) Several commentators appreciated the additional time for acceptance speeches, following criticism at the previous ceremony.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) *[Kotaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kotaku "Kotaku")*'s Zack Zwiezen considered Statler and Waldorf the highlight for their humorous interjections and heckles directed at Keighley,[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Kotaku_Muppets-127) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur felt their appearance acknowledged the show's issues without addressing them.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)

Many considered the Game Changer award and Amir Satvat's emotional acceptance speech the show's highlight;[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_Winners-71)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-WP_Review-114) *Rolling Stone*'s Van der Velde thought the award meant Keighley was taking criticism seriously,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Review-117) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur and Henley felt its introduction in the same year as Future Class's removal gave the appearance of awarding individuals to reduce the voice of a collective group.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Satvat-129) Some Future Class members were concerned the award had replaced the program as "it's easier to control one person's message than the message of multiple years Future Class members".[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Future_Class-130) Some viewers suggested Satvat's role at [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent") made him "part of the problem" with layoffs.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Aftermath_Future_Class-130)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Satvat-131) Four days after the show, Satvat said he had received "countless hateful messages", including [antisemitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitic "Antisemitic") comments directed at his wife.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Satvat-131)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Eurogamer_Satvat-132) Journalists praised [Swen Vincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swen_Vincke "Swen Vincke")'s speech criticizing publishers who chase "arbitrary sales targets" instead of making games "they want to play".[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-BBC_Winners-71)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Digital_Trends_Review-93)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Muppets-128)

Some viewers interpreted Vincke's comments as criticism of *Black Myth: Wukong*, which was partially attributed to a poor Chinese translation of his speech; some subsequently attempted to [review bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_bomb "Review bomb") Vincke's game, *[Baldur's Gate 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_3 "Baldur's Gate 3")*, on Steam,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Vincke-133)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Vincke-134) as well as *Astro Bot* on Metacritic.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-NME_Ji-135) [Alanah Pearce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alanah_Pearce "Alanah Pearce") said that a *Black Myth: Wukong* developer cried after failing to win Game of the Year,[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Eurogamer_Ji-136)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VGC_Ji-137) though former *[IGN China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN_China "IGN China")* editor-in-chief Charles Young said he was with the developers at the show and none cried.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Gamereactor_Ji-138)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Yahoo_Ji-139)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Ji-140) Following the ceremony, the game's producer Feng Ji expressed disappointment over the loss and confusion about the award's criteria, writing "I feel like I came all the way here for nothing!";[[n]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-142) he said he had written his acceptance speech two years ### Viewership

An estimated 154 million viewers watched the ceremony, the most in the show's history to date[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Views-1) and a 31% increase from the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5) Its figures surpassed the average viewers of the [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII") by 30 million, the Academy Awards sevenfold, the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards") ninefold, and the [World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Series "2024 World Series") tenfold.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) Referencing the viewing figures, [Reggie Fils-Aimé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Fils-Aimé "Reggie Fils-Aimé") called the show "the biggest global entertainment event of our time",[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Push_Square_Viewers-151) though *TheGamer*'s Kaur considered the claim disingenuous, citing the [FIFA World Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_finals "FIFA World Cup finals") and [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), and the fact that shows like the Super Bowl are generally viewed in groups rather than individually.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-TheGamer_Viewers-152)

According to *Streams Charts*, the ceremony peaked at over four million concurrent viewers—the most in its history to date and a 10% increase from 2023—across 1,498 channels, including 1.25 million viewers on the official YouTube broadcast and 397,000 on Twitch.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-5)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-Game_Rant_Streams-153) More than 15,900 content creators co-streamed the event, including over 11,000 on Twitch and a record 4,500 on YouTube.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-VentureBeat_Viewers-150) On YouTube, the ceremony peaked at 2.17 million concurrent viewers (a 28% increase), with over 1.3 million on the official channel (a 35% increase).[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-GamesIndustry_Viewers-154) On Twitter, usage of the [hashtag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashtag "Hashtag") #TheGameAwards increased by 150%, with more than 1.59 million posts receiving 6.79 billion [impressions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impression_(online_media) "Impression (online media)").[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2024#cite_note-ANN_Viewers-155)

# [2403.18140] Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.18140) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2)
> Abstract:The high compute cost associated with pretraining large language models limits their research. Two strategies have emerged to address this issue: domain specialization and pretraining with high-quality data. To explore these strategies, we specialized the Mistral-7B model with 1.9 billion unique tokens from reputable Brazilian legal sources and conducted few-shot evaluations on legal and general knowledge test suites. Our model, Juru, demonstrates the benefits of domain specialization by achieving improved performance on legal benchmarks, even with a reduced amount of pretraining data. However, this domain specialization through continued pretraining comes at the cost of increased forgetting in unrelated domains, as evidenced by performance degradation on general knowledge test suites in both Portuguese and English. This study contributes to the growing body of scientific evidence showing that pretraining data selection may enhance the performance of large language models, enabling the exploration of these models at a lower cost. Juru is publicly available at [this https URL](https://huggingface.co/roseval/Juru-7B) .

# Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources

Roseval Malaquias Junior Affiliation: Computer Science Department, University of São Paulo, São Carlos, São Paulo, Brazil  
, E-mail <roseval@usp.br> Affiliation: Maritaca AI, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil E-mail [{ramon, rodrigo}@maritaca.ai](mailto:%7Bramon,%20rodrigo%7D@maritaca.ai) Ramon Pires Roseli A. F. Romero Affiliation: Computer Science Department, University of São Paulo, São Carlos, São Paulo, Brazil  
, E-mail <roseval@usp.br> Rodrigo Nogueira E-mail <rafrance@icmc.usp.br> Affiliation: Maritaca AI, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil E-mail [{ramon, rodrigo}@maritaca.ai](mailto:%7Bramon,%20rodrigo%7D@maritaca.ai)

###### Abstract

The high compute cost associated with pretraining large language models limits their research. Two strategies have emerged to address this issue: domain specialization and pretraining with high-quality data. To explore these strategies, we specialized the Mistral-7B model with 1.9 billion unique tokens from reputable Brazilian legal sources and conducted few-shot evaluations on legal and general knowledge test suites. Our model, Juru, demonstrates the benefits of domain specialization by achieving improved performance on legal benchmarks, even with a reduced amount of pretraining data. However, this domain specialization through continued pretraining comes at the cost of increased forgetting in unrelated domains, as evidenced by performance degradation on general knowledge test suites in both Portuguese and English. This study contributes to the growing body of scientific evidence showing that pretraining data selection may enhance the performance of large language models, enabling the exploration of these models at a lower cost. Juru is publicly available at <https://huggingface.co/roseval/Juru-7B>.

###### Keywords:

Domain Specialization Continued Pretraining Legal Language Models Low-Resource Pretraining

## 1 Introduction

Large Language Models (LLMs) are commonly trained on vast amounts of general-purpose data sourced from internet snapshots, such as the CommonCrawl [[3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib3 ""), [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib4 ""), [32](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib32 "")] and C4 [[32](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib32 ""), [34](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib34 "")]. Scaling laws [[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib14 "")] support this paradigm, suggesting more capable models with increased data and trainable parameters. As a result, LLMs developed through this method demonstrate the ability to address tasks across multiple languages and domains [[20](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib20 "")].

The significant computational resources required for pretraining with such massive datasets pose a challenge for research, limiting the exploration of their capabilities. However, it is possible to observe competitive results on a smaller scale through the application of continued pretraining.
In the literature, the selection of domain-specific data [[8](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib8 ""), [9](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib9 ""), [22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib22 "")] from reputable sources [[12](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib12 ""), [18](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib18 ""), [21](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib21 "")] stands out.

The large general-purpose pretraining of LLMs promotes general factual knowledge and language comprehension. Therefore, continued pretraining on the same scale and scope might not be necessary to improve LLMs’ performance.
By employing domain-specific data from reputable sources, we postulate that an LLM initially trained on general-purpose data can improve its performance in a specific domain with minimal additional data, although this may come at the expense of performance degradation in other domains.

To test this hypothesis, we specialized the Mistral-7B [[15](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib15 "")] model for the Brazilian legal domain, using <!-- MathML: <math alttext="1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S1.p4.m1"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.91.9 billion unique tokens sourced mainly from academic studies from reputable sources. The resulting model, Juru, was evaluated on multiple-choice test suites covering both Brazilian legal knowledge and general knowledge domains. Our objective is to assess the impact of incorporating exclusively domain-specific data during continued pretraining on the model’s performance.

Across the proposed pretraining, our model demonstrated enhanced performance on the legal test suite, while exhibiting a decrease in performance on the general knowledge test suites. In particular, a more pronounced decrease was observed on the English test suite compared to the Portuguese one, suggesting that previously acquired knowledge is better retained when it shares greater similarity with the target domain of specialization. These results contribute to the growing body of scientific evidence supporting the effectiveness of specialized pretraining for improving the performance of generalist models on specific domains. Such specialization may facilitate their research by reducing the compute cost associated with training. Additionally, the resulting model, Juru, is publicly released to support further research on domain specialization through continued pretraining. To the best of our knowledge, Juru is the first LLM pretrained for the Brazilian legal domain.

## 2 Related Work

The increasing scale of LLMs, in both parameter numbers and training data, has led to the emergence of previously unseen abilities in smaller-scale models [[33](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib33 "")]. Recent advances have enabled these models to achieve human-level performance across various tasks that require textual comprehension, specialized knowledge, mathematical reasoning, multilingualism, programming, and image interpretation [[20](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib20 "")]. With such results, it is arguable that these models demonstrate the capacity to integrate these diverse skills in a cohesive manner.

Language and domain specialization have become effective strategies for ensuring that LLMs bring tangible benefits in real-world applications. Recent works have shown that continued pretrained in language-specific corpora, particularly in Portuguese [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib1 ""), [17](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib17 ""), [22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib22 "")], enhances significantly the performance of downstream tasks without the need to increase the parameter count.

The Brazilian legal field emerges as a relevant example of such domain specialization, as previous studies have underscored the performance of language models pretrained on legal corpora [[9](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib9 ""), [24](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib24 "")].
However, those models are encoder-only, lacking the ability to generate text sequentially, which is essential for several legal applications.

SaulLM-7B [[8](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib8 "")] is the first LLM pretrained to tackle the nuances of legal languages and follow instructions to support conversation interactions. Starting from Mistral-7B [[15](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib15 "")], the model was pretrained on 30 billion tokens of an English legal dataset. In a subsequent study, Colombo et al. [[7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib7 "")] scaled this approach to a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. The authors continually pretrained Mixtral-54B and Mixtral-141B on 540 billion tokens of English legal texts, producing SaulLM-54B and SaulLM-141B. While these larger models achieve higher performance on most in-domain tasks, their increased size correlates with lower performance on certain legal tasks.

To the best of our knowledge, Juru is the first LLM pretrained for the Brazilian legal domain. Our experiments show that, relative to its base model, Juru achieves superior performance on in-domain tasks. However, its performance deteriorates on tasks beyond the Brazilian legal domain.

## 3 Methodology

In this section, we describe the gathering and curation of data from public sources within the Brazilian legal domain, as well as the pretraining of the Juru model, including its base model, hyperparameters, and optimization methods.

### 3.1 Pretraining Data

We conducted web scraping of academic papers in Portuguese within the Brazilian legal domain, prioritizing data with educational value.

Academic papers were scraped from various reputable sources that catalog research from Brazilian higher education institutions and national journals. Each platform offers filters for extracting Brazilian papers exclusively in Portuguese, accessible for non-commercial distribution. Also, we scraped the LexML11 1 [https://www.lexml.gov.br](https://www.lexml.gov.br/ "") database, focusing on a subset of Brazilian federal laws.

A total of 13,278 documents were extracted from academic paper databases. Nearly <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="99\%" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS1.p3.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>99</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 99%99\% of these documents are in Portable Document Format (PDF). Hence, we used Marker22 2 <https://github.com/VikParuchuri/marker> for extracting text from these documents.

Texts from 14,743 federal laws were extracted from the LexML database. Additionally, the dataset from the study by Sakiyama et al. [[27](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib27 "")] was added to the pretraining dataset, consisting of 32,535 legal documents distributed between decisions and judgments from the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court.

After extracting the documents, they were automatically curated using the filter proposed by Rae et al. [[25](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib25 "")], adapted for Portuguese. This filter removes documents that are unlikely to be predominantly natural language, such as tables or long lists, as they could hinder the learning process of the LLM.

Table 1: Distribution of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) [[29](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib29 "")] tokens for the pretraining dataset, using the Mistral-7B tokenizer.

Considering the tokenizer of Mistral-7B, the model employed in our pretraining, we gathered <!-- MathML: <math alttext="1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS1.p6.m1"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.91.9 billion tokens, as shown in Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3.1 Pretraining Data ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources"). Each document was divided into sequences of 4,096 tokens.

### 3.2 Juru Model

The Juru model extends the causal language modeling pretraining of a Mistral-7B model, without instruction finetuning. We employed the t5x and seqio frameworks [[26](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib26 "")] for the proposed pretraining.

Although more recent models [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib10 ""), [11](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib11 "")] of comparable size have demonstrated superior performance compared to Mistral-7B, we chose Mistral-7B due to its earlier release date. This decision aims to reduce the risk of data contamination in our test suites.

For the pretraining hyperparameters, we employed the AdaFactor optimizer [[30](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib30 "")] without factorization, with a first-order momentum of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="0.9" display="inline" id="S3.SS2.p3.m1"><semantics><mn>0.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 0.90.9 and a second-order momentum of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="1-k^{-0.8}" id="S3.SS2.p3.m2"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-k^{-0.8}</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1−k−0.81-k^{-0.8}, where <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="k" display="inline" id="S3.SS2.p3.m3"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> --> kk represents the current training step. Additionally, we applied dynamic weight decay by <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="lr^{2}" display="inline" id="S3.SS2.p3.m4"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">lr^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> --> l​r2lr^{2}, with <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="lr" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS2.p3.m5"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">lr</annotation></semantics></math> --> l​rlr as the current learning rate value, and global norm clipping of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="1.0" id="S3.SS2.p3.m6"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.01.0.

In addition to the loss associated with the causal language modeling task, we used an auxiliary loss of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="10^{-4}\log^{2}\left(\sum_{i}e^{z_{i}}\right)" display="inline" id="S3.SS2.p4.m1"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}\log^{2}\left(\sum_{i}e^{z_{i}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> --> 10−4​log2⁡(∑iezi)10^{-4}\log^{2}\left(\sum_{i}e^{z_{i}}\right), where <!-- MathML: <math alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS2.p4.m2"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> --> zz denotes the logits of the prediction. This auxiliary loss helps dampen the values of the pretraining loss. The learning rate is initially set at <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="0" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS2.p4.m3"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> --> 00 and gradually increases during a linear warm-up period of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="250" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S3.SS2.p4.m4"><semantics><mn>250</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">250</annotation></semantics></math> --> 250250 training steps until it reaches <!-- MathML: <math alttext="0.001" intent=":literal" display="inline" id="S3.SS2.p4.m5"><semantics><mn>0.001</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.001</annotation></semantics></math> --> 0.0010.001. ## 4 Evaluation

Evaluating LLMs for text generation poses challenges due to the subjective nature of emerging skills such as natural language understanding and domain expertise, alongside their ability to integrate these skills for problem-solving. Given their broad capabilities, evaluating with open-ended questioning provides insights into the models’ knowledge representation and their capacity to generate human-like responses [[35](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib35 "")].

However, the evaluation of responses to open-ended questions poses inherent difficulties. Human evaluation is resource-intensive, requiring expertise in specific domain tasks and training in evaluation methodology for experimental robustness. Additionally, relying solely on SOTA LLMs for evaluation may yield a low correlation with human judges due to specific vocabulary and knowledge of a target domain. Hence, there’s an increasing emphasis on evaluating these models using standardized multiple-choice exams, such as those used in university admission processes [[2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib2 ""), [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib5 ""), [19](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib19 ""), [23](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib23 ""), [28](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib28 "")]. Such exams cover diverse topics and skills, proving advantageous for LLM evaluation.

We investigate how continued pretraining through domain specialization influences both knowledge learning and forgetting. Hence, we evaluate the specialized Juru model on three standardized multiple-choice test suites: Brazilian legal knowledge, representing the target domain of our specialization; Portuguese general knowledge, which share the same language as the target domain but do not assess legal knowledge; and English general knowledge, whose distribution is closer to the original English-centric training data of Mistral-7B.

For all test suites, we adopt accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. We group all editions of the same exam administered within a given year into a single evaluation group. When aggregating multiple exams, we report the mean accuracy. Lastly, we employ few-shot learning with three examples during our evaluation, as the model was trained solely for text completion and did not undergo any instruction finetuning.

### 4.1 Brazilian Legal Knowledge

For evaluating the Juru model, we used questions from six Bar Association Exams (OAB) of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" display="inline" alttext="2024" id="S4.SS1.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>2024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2024</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20242024 and <!-- MathML: <math alttext="2023" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS1.p1.m2"><semantics><mn>2023</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2023</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20232023, and two National Judiciary Exams (ENAM) of <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="2024" display="inline" id="S4.SS1.p1.m3"><semantics><mn>2024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2024</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20242024. The OAB exam is mandatory for all law graduates aspiring to practice law in Brazil. It comprises two phases; the initial phase encompasses <!-- MathML: <math alttext="80" intent=":literal" display="inline" id="S4.SS1.p1.m4"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> --> 8080 multiple-choice questions, while the second phase consists of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS1.p1.m5"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> --> 44 essay questions and the creation of a procedural document. ENAM was introduced in 2023 to unify the selection process for entry into the Brazilian judiciary. As of its implementation, only candidates who have passed the ENAM within the last two years are eligible to apply for judicial positions in Brazil. This exam includes a single phase with <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="80" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS1.p1.m6"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> --> 8080 multiple-choice questions. We included only multiple-choice questions from the <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="2023" display="inline" id="S4.SS1.p1.m7"><semantics><mn>2023</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2023</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20232023 and <!-- MathML: <math intent=":literal" alttext="2024" display="inline" id="S4.SS1.p1.m8"><semantics><mn>2024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2024</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20242024 OAB, and <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="2024" id="S4.SS1.p1.m9"><semantics><mn>2024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2024</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20242024 ENAM exams, comprising a total set of <!-- MathML: <math alttext="638" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S4.SS1.p1.m10"><semantics><mn>638</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">638</annotation></semantics></math> --> 638638 questions, as illustrated in Table [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 4.1 Brazilian Legal Knowledge ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources").

### 4.2 Portuguese General Knowledge

Pires et al. [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib22 "")] observed a performance degradation on English benchmarks following the specialization of an English-centric LLM for Portuguese. These results raise the following question: Is catastrophic forgetting limited to cross-linguistic domain specialization, or does specializing in a specific domain within a single language also lead to forgetting of general knowledge in that language?

To address this question, we examined the impact of specializing the Juru model in the Brazilian legal domain on its performance in Portuguese general knowledge tasks, using the multiple-choice exams listed in Table [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S4.T3 "Table 3 ‣ 4.2 Portuguese General Knowledge ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources"), comprising a total amount of 2,123 questions.

Table 3: Configuration of Portuguese general knowledge test suite.

Following Almeida et al. [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib1 "")], we ignore all the questions that require image understanding. Some exams have captions describing the image contents. In those cases, we incorporate them into the exact position the images would appear.

### 4.3 English General Knowledge

Unlike the Sabiá [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib22 "")] model, which underwent extensive continued pretraining, the Juru model was trained for fewer steps due to the smaller size of its legal specialization dataset. While Pires et al. [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib22 "")] observed a loss of English knowledge in their model after extended training on Portuguese data, their experiments involved a significantly longer training regime and a more diverse dataset. This raises another question: Can shorter, domain-specific pretraining mitigate or prevent catastrophic forgetting of previously learned knowledge?

To investigate this, we evaluated the Juru model on the MMLU benchmark [[13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib13 "")], a widely used test suite for assessing general knowledge and reasoning abilities in English [[15](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib15 ""), [20](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib20 ""), [31](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib31 "")]. While MMLU includes a broad range of subjects, such as STEM, humanities, law, and medicine, we restricted our evaluation to the college-level and high school-level subsets, amounting to 4,369 questions, as outlined in Table [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S4.T4 "Table 4 ‣ 4.3 English General Knowledge ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources").

## 5 Results

The proposed test suites were used to track the model’s performance across checkpoints during continued pretraining. Figure [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S5.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 5 Results ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources") presents the accuracy as a function of the number of tokens processed during continued pretraining. Each epoch comprises <!-- MathML: <math alttext="1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.91.9 billion tokens from Brazilian legal texts. The 0B point corresponds to the base Mistral-7B model, while the checkpoint at 7.1B tokens represents the specialized Juru model.

Figure 1: Accuracy on the Brazilian legal knowledge, English general knowledge, and Portuguese general knowledge test suites during continued pretraining.

The results support the study’s central hypothesis: as the LLM undergoes domain specialization, performance improves on in-domain tasks but declines on out-of-domain general knowledge tasks. Upon analyzing the curves, we observed the model’s accuracy on the legal test suite steadily increased, peaking at <!-- MathML: <math alttext="49.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.p2.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>49.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 49.2%49.2\% on 7.1B tokens. In contrast, performance on general knowledge test suites decreased relative to the base model, with final accuracies of <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="48.1\%" id="S5.p2.m2"><semantics><mrow><mn>48.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48.1\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 48.1%48.1\% for the Portuguese knowledge test suite and <!-- MathML: <math alttext="58.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal" id="S5.p2.m3"><semantics><mrow><mn>58.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 58.0%58.0\% for the English knowledge test suite at the same checkpoint.

Overall, the optimal version of Juru was obtained at 7.1B tokens, corresponding to the highest accuracy on the legal knowledge test suite. All subsequent analyses are based on this checkpoint, which we refer to as Juru. The next subsection compares the performance of this final model to the base Mistral-7B model across both legal and general knowledge test suites.

Table [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S5.T5 "Table 5 ‣ 5.1 Results per Benchmark ‣ 5 Results ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources") shows that Juru outperforms the base Mistral-7B model across all legal benchmarks, with an overall gain of approximately 4.7% in average accuracy. The most notable improvement is observed in the ENAM-2024 benchmark, with a gain of 5.6%. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of domain specialization through continued pretraining in enhancing performance on legal knowledge tasks.

While Mistral-7B achieves higher scores on both the college and high school subsets of MMLU, Juru underperforms across the board, resulting in a 3.6% decrease in the overall average accuracy.

### 5.2 Results Analysis

The results demonstrate the dynamics of learning domain-specific knowledge for the specialization of the Juru model. Specialization in the Brazilian legal domain yielded an increase of <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="4.7\%" intent=":literal" id="S5.SS2.p1.m1"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> --> 4.7%4.7\% accuracy compared to Mistral-7B in the Brazilian legal knowledge test suite, despite the relatively small training dataset of only <!-- MathML: <math alttext="1.9" intent=":literal" display="inline" id="S5.SS2.p1.m2"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.91.9 billion unique tokens.

In line with the hypothesis of this study, specialization has led to a decline in the model’s capacity to solve tasks beyond its specialized domain. Despite the shared language among evaluated tasks on the legal and Portuguese general test suites, specialization in only one knowledge domain has resulted in decreased performance in other domain areas. Clear correlations between types of knowledge areas and degradation were not evident, as shown in Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#S5.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Results per Benchmark ‣ 5 Results ‣ Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources"). Furthermore, when comparing the decline in performance across the Portuguese and English general knowledge test suites, the Juru model exhibited a greater degree of forgetting on the English suite. This pattern suggests that knowledge forgetting is influenced by the similarity between the evaluated and specialized domains: the less similar the previously learned knowledge is to the target domain, the greater the degree of forgetting.

We posit that further pretraining of the Juru model is likely to increase the disparity between legal and general knowledge curves. Consequently, while performance in legal-related tasks may increase, there would likely be a significant decrease in performance in specific knowledge domains that require different skill sets.

## 6 Limitations

While positive results are evident, there’s a possible risk of contamination in the pretraining dataset. This risk arises from web scraping pretraining data in the latter half of <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" alttext="2023" intent=":literal" id="S6.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>2023</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2023</annotation></semantics></math> --> 20232023, after the publication of the OAB-2023 and MMLU exams. Although the dataset was primarily sourced from reputable Brazilian academic and legal documents, and it is unlikely to contain the test questions, the risk of indirect contamination cannot be fully ruled out. To address this, we plan to include newly released exams from 2025 and 2026 in future evaluations.

All experiments reported in this paper are based on a specific subset of Brazilian legal data. Whether the observed trends generalize to other subdomains or other types of data than those originated from reputable sources remains an open question. Exploring a broader range of legal corpora, including news articles, blogs, and jurisprudential commentaries, may reveal different specialization behaviors.

Our work is subject to the same validity challenges commonly faced in the evaluation of LLMs, as noted in prior studies [[8](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib8 ""), [10](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib10 ""), [11](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2#bib.bib11 "")]. In the Brazilian context, what constitutes legal proficiency? Is it the ability to recall legislation, generate legally sound summaries, or predict judicial decisions? We argue that these skills are interrelated. Therefore, improving performance on one legal task may correlate with improvements in others, as they often rely on overlapping capabilities. We do not claim that Juru excels across all legal language processing tasks. Rather, we use performance on Brazilian legal standardized exams, designed to assess human legal competence, as a practical proxy for specialization effectiveness. The observed improvements on these benchmarks suggest that domain specialization may transfer to a broader range of legal tasks.

## 7 Conclusions and Future Work

In this study, we introduced Juru, the first LLM specialized in the Brazilian legal domain, pretrained on <!-- MathML: <math display="inline" intent=":literal" alttext="1.9" id="S7.p1.m1"><semantics><mn>1.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.9</annotation></semantics></math> --> 1.91.9 billion unique tokens. Despite its smaller size and limited data, we observed an expressive improvement in the model’s ability to resolve multiple-choice questions within the Brazilian legal domain. Our findings confirm that domain specialization can be an efficient strategy for improving LLM performance at a lower compute cost. However, this comes with a trade-off: diminished performance on tasks unrelated to the target domain.

Additionally, the comparison between Portuguese and English general test suites revealed a more pronounced decline in the English benchmarks. This suggests that the extent of forgetting may be linked to domain similarity: the lower the similarity the previously acquired knowledge has to the specialized domain, the higher the risk of forgetting.

For future work, our primary aim is to incorporate evaluations of the Juru model with new benchmarks that fall outside the model’s knowledge cut-off to mitigate the possibility of data contamination. A promising direction is to investigate whether aggregating domains with high similarity during continued pretraining could enhance specialization performance without catastrophic forgetting of previously learned knowledge. Deeper understanding of these dynamics may lead to the development of LLMs with less compute through targeted domain specialization. We also release all Juru checkpoints from the experiments presented in this paper to further support future research on these topics, particularly within the Brazilian legal domain.
